sha_binding.verified_source_note: Last commit on this branch touching a non-proof path; it carries the complete substantive change. merge_sha is null pre-merge as the shared evidence contract requires (CEP-E7) -- a branch SHA must never be represented as a merge SHA. post-merge-lane-close.yml binds it to the real merge commit via proof-generate rebindEvidenceJsonSha, and the same workflow harvests runtime_proof from the Writable DB proof (staging only) receipt. evidence_commit_sha and current_pr_head_sha are resolved by CI.

gate_results.detail: OUTBOX_TRACK_ONLY_CHOKEPOINT_GUARD refuses outbox.enqueue for a Track Only pick in BOTH InMemoryOutboxRepository and DatabaseOutboxRepository. Every delivery path funnels through this call, so a route that omits its own check still cannot create delivery work. Mutation control removes both marked blocks (the regex carries the g flag; an earlier revision removed only the first and proved half the feature).

ATOMIC_TRACK_ONLY_CHOKEPOINT_GUARD refuses enqueueDistributionAtomic before the RPC is issued. Proven by the recorded RPC call list being empty at baseline and ['enqueue_distribution_atomic'] in the mutant -- the absence of the database call, not an exception message.

DatabaseOutboxRepository.loadPickMetadata refuses to proceed when the pick row is absent or the query errors. An unreadable row means Track Only status cannot be established, which is not the same as 'not Track Only'.

Submit, requeue, retry and the pre-atomic run-audit path each carry an independently mutation-proven guard: TRACK_ONLY_DIRECT_ENQUEUE_GUARD, TRACK_ONLY_REQUEUE_GUARD, TRACK_ONLY_RETRY_GUARD, TRACK_ONLY_ATOMIC_GUARD. Defence in depth above the chokepoint.
TRACK_ONLY_REQUEST_INTEGRITY_GUARD refuses to answer a Track Only request with a delivery-eligible pick -- the persisted pre-atomic enforcement the contract names.

RECAP_TRACK_ONLY_EXCLUSION_GUARD excludes Track Only picks from recap top-play selection. Added after round-3 review found the outbox chokepoint would otherwise throw inside postRecapSummary (whose enqueue sits outside its own try block, with topPlayRow chosen purely by profit and no Track Only filter), silently killing daily and weekly recaps.

ZOMBIE_HEALTH_TRACK_ONLY_EXCLUSION_GUARD keeps a Track Only pick out of the zombie-health predicate. Confirmed in source that a Track Only submission lands as promotion_status=qualified, promotion_target=best-bets, lifecycle=validated -- matching every clause of that predicate. Without the guard /health reports 503 after the first legitimate capper submission and prescribes a requeue TRACK_ONLY_REQUEUE_GUARD refuses. Mutation-controlled.

BOARD_CAPACITY_TRACK_ONLY_EXCLUSION_GUARD keeps a Track Only pick out of live board capacity in both getPromotionBoardState implementations. Otherwise it inflates board, sport, game and duplicate counts for the full 7-day window and suppresses genuinely deliverable picks once a cap is reached. Proven by premise assertion plus a positive control rather than a mutation control -- see static_proof.controls.coverage.
CAPPER_TRACK_ONLY_PIN_GUARD pins distributionMode='track-only' server-side for an authenticated capper; the mutant shows the client can otherwise opt into member delivery.
CAPPER_SOURCE_PIN_GUARD pins the pick source server-side; the mutant shows an authenticated capper can otherwise spoof it.

SMART_FORM_HTTP_CONTRACT_GUARD refuses any HTTP source:'smart-form' submission that does not declare both metadata.distributionMode and metadata.participantResolution. Closes the SMART_FORM_TRIGGER_SCOPE exemption at the boundary for operator/submitter roles and for the fail-open BYPASS_CONTEXT, whose role is operator.

SMART_FORM_RELATIONSHIP_GUARD refuses cross-sport event injection, participants outside the canonical event, ID/display-name mismatch, a player assigned to an incompatible team, duplicate sides, and alias-based duplicate sides submitted through participantId vs canonicalId for one entity.

CANONICAL_SPORT_ID_GUARD refuses a sportId the catalog does not carry. Every reference-data lookup is case-sensitive, so without it a sportId of 'nba' searches an empty universe and the coverage proof reports success while proving nothing. Live sports ids (NBA, NFL, MLB, NHL, NCAAB, NCAAF, Soccer, MMA, Tennis) match V1_REFERENCE_DATA exactly and the form sources its values from GET /api/reference-data/catalog, so the case-sensitive comparison matches by construction.

MANUAL_COVERAGE_GAP_PROOF_GUARD verifies the claimed gap rather than accepting it: refuses zero participants; refuses a one-sided matchup for TEAM_SPORTS only (individual sports have legitimate one-participant markets); refuses a name still holding a non-ASCII code point after folding; refuses duplicates by alias key; refuses any participant that resolves canonically. Round-4 fix: the check now consults the catalog (participants, 124 teams, populated) before searchTeams/searchPlayers (teams and player_team_assignments, both 0 rows in production) -- a search-only proof returned null for every name in every sport and accepted every override.

Proven against Cyrillic and Greek homoglyphs, fullwidth forms, zero-width characters in every word, punctuation on single-word names, and city-prefix asymmetry in both directions. LATIN_EXPANSION covers the Latin letters NFKD does not decompose so real Soccer clubs (Brondby IF, Preussen Munster, Kasimpasa, LKS Lodz) are admitted rather than refused as non-Latin.

SMART_FORM_TRIGGER_SCOPE keys the strict contract on the presence of Smart Form fields so pre-existing in-process smart-form callers keep working. Its mutation control asserts a regression the guard prevents (legacy callers refused 422) rather than a bypass it blocks.

controls.method: Each control reads the guard's own source, deletes the block between its UTV2-1672 <NAME>_START / _END markers by regex (g flag, so a guard marking multiple blocks is fully removed), asserts mutantSource !== source so a rename cannot make the control vacuous, writes a sibling module, imports it with a ?mutation= cache-buster, asserts the prevented behaviour now occurs, and unlinks in finally.
controls.coverage: 16 of 17 UTV2-1672 guards have a mutation control; removal fails and restoration passes for each. BOARD_CAPACITY_TRACK_ONLY_EXCLUSION_GUARD lives in packages/db/src/runtime-repositories.ts, which an app test cannot import as source without violating the db-client-boundary check; it is instead proven by asserting its premise (the pick really is promotion_status=qualified, promotion_target=best-bets, lifecycle=validated -- exactly what the board query counts) plus a positive control showing an ordinary qualified pick still counts 1. Weaker than a mutation control and labelled as such.

independent_review.scope: rounds 2-4 adversarially reviewed the implementation; each round also audited the previous round's fixes
independent_review.outcome: all outage-class and vacuity-class findings fixed through five rounds; two classes deliberately carried as disclosed residual risk. Round 5 (Codex reviewer on PR #1466) raised three findings: two P1 confirmed in source and fixed (zombie-health and live-board capacity both count a Track Only pick, which is force-qualified to best-bets and never enqueued), one P2 deliberately deferred.
not_fixed: isSameEntityName both under-refuses (a trailing extra or reordered token evades it: 'Knicks Basketball', 'Knicks NY') and over-refuses (a shared trailing token matches distinct entities: 'North Texas' refused as 'Texas'). Not independently fixable: round 3 required 'Alex Pereira Junior' NOT be treated as covered while round 4 requires 'Knicks Basketball' BE treated as covered -- the same structural case with opposite required verdicts. This is bypass-detection for a manual-override claim, not a safety boundary: it does not gate Track Only, member distribution, capper identity, or source spoofing, and a wrong verdict creates no member delivery.
getCatalog() is an uncached 7-query round trip on every Smart Form submission. Performance debt.

P2: DatabaseReferenceDataRepository.searchPlayers fetches an unordered global limit*5 batch matching %query% and only then filters by sport assignment, so a sport absent from that arbitrary batch is reported playersAvailable:false even when canonical players exist -- a fail-open that would enable the form's coverage-gap fallback. Confirmed real in source. Deferred because it is latent (it needs >500 players across sports; production has 12) and a correct fix changes the pagination and scoping semantics of a shared repository method other callers depend on -- the same shape of change that made rounds 2 and 3 introduce new defects. The review thread is left open rather than resolved.
disclosed_dependencies: apps/smart-form on this branch sends neither metadata.distributionMode nor metadata.participantResolution, so SMART_FORM_HTTP_CONTRACT_GUARD 400s the current frontend until Lane 2 (UTV2-1786) lands. Intended phased outcome -- production activation is disabled, and the alternative is leaving the HTTP boundary open.

teams and player_team_assignments are empty in production AND staging. The catalog-backed branch (participants, 124 teams) is what makes the coverage guard non-vacuous today; the search-backed branch becomes load-bearing only once those tables are populated. Backfilling is production data mutation -- a hard stop for this lane.

runtime_proof.defect_fixed: Smart Form had no server-side Track Only enforcement: the client declared distribution intent, capper identity and pick source were accepted from the payload, and participant resolution was unverified. Every backend path that can create member delivery work is now pinned closed for a Track Only pick, identity is derived server-side, and a manual coverage-gap claim is verified against reference data rather than trusted.
runtime_proof.measurement_basis: In-process measurement against the real modules, plus mutation controls that delete a guard's marked block from a copy of its own source and execute the mutant. Live Postgres is exercised separately by the required verify job's test:live-db half in the staging-ci environment; these probes measure this lane's own behaviour, which is what the guards claim.

queries.name: outbox chokepoint refuses delivery work for a Track Only pick
queries.method: OUTBOX_TRACK_ONLY_CHOKEPOINT_GUARD exercised through both InMemoryOutboxRepository.enqueue and DatabaseOutboxRepository.enqueue, the latter against a stub Supabase client modelling .from('picks').select().eq().maybeSingle() and .from().insert().select().single()
queries.result: enqueue refused in both implementations; zero delivery_outbox inserts observed. A delivery-eligible pick still inserts, so the refusal is specific rather than a repository that now writes nothing.
queries.significance: This is the chokepoint every delivery path funnels through, so a route that omits its own check still cannot create member delivery.

queries.name: atomic distribution path is refused before the RPC is issued
queries.method: ATOMIC_TRACK_ONLY_CHOKEPOINT_GUARD measured by recording the RPC call list rather than catching an exception
queries.result: baseline rpcCalls === []; with the guard block deleted, rpcCalls === ['enqueue_distribution_atomic']
queries.significance: Proven by the absence of the database call itself, not by an error message that could be thrown for any reason.

queries.name: an unreadable pick row is refused rather than treated as deliverable
queries.method: DatabaseOutboxRepository.loadPickMetadata driven with an absent row and with a query error
queries.result: both refused with an explicit message; neither fell through to enqueue
queries.significance: Fail-closed: an unreadable row means Track Only status cannot be established, which is not the same as 'not Track Only'.

queries.name: Track Only picks do not occupy live board capacity
queries.method: getPromotionBoardState after a real processSubmission of a Track Only pick, asserting its promotion state first (promotion_status=qualified, promotion_target=best-bets, lifecycle=validated) so the probe cannot pass vacuously
queries.result: currentBoardCount 0, sameSportCount 0, sameGameCount 0, duplicateCount 0; an ordinary qualified pick still counts 1
queries.significance: Without the exclusion these picks hold board capacity for 7 days and suppress genuinely deliverable picks once a cap is reached.

queries.name: a Track Only pick is not reported as a zombie
queries.method: checkZombiePickHealth over the same submission, with a mutation control removing the exclusion
queries.result: baseline count 0 status healthy; mutant count 1 status down with a remediation matching /requeue/
queries.significance: The mutant's prescribed remediation is refused by TRACK_ONLY_REQUEUE_GUARD, so without this /health raises an alarm operators cannot resolve.

queries.name: a Track Only pick is excluded from recap aggregation
queries.method: computeRecapSummary with a settled Track Only pick holding the best result, plus a mutation control
queries.result: baseline settledCount 1 and the Track Only pick is not topPlay; mutant settledCount 2 and it becomes topPlay
queries.significance: postRecapSummary enqueues the top play outside its own try block, so absent this the outbox chokepoint would throw and silently kill daily and weekly recaps.

queries.name: manual coverage-gap claims are verified against populated reference data
queries.method: MANUAL_COVERAGE_GAP_PROOF_GUARD with searchTeams and searchPlayers both stubbed to return [] -- reproducing production, where teams and player_team_assignments are empty
queries.result: the canonical name is still refused, via the catalog branch (participants, 124 teams)
queries.significance: A search-only proof returned null for every name in every sport and accepted every override while appearing to work.

queries.name: identity and source are server-derived, not client-declared
queries.method: CAPPER_TRACK_ONLY_PIN_GUARD, CAPPER_SOURCE_PIN_GUARD and SMART_FORM_HTTP_CONTRACT_GUARD exercised over the real HTTP surface, each with a mutation control
queries.result: baseline refuses the spoofed source, refuses opting into member delivery, and refuses a Smart Form submission missing its contract fields; each mutant permits the corresponding bypass
queries.significance: Establishes that the pins are load-bearing rather than incidental to some other check.

runtime_proof.mutation_testing: 16 controls, all killed. Each deletes a guard's marked block from a copy of its own source, asserts the mutated text actually differs (so a rename cannot make the control vacuous), imports the mutant with a cache-buster and asserts the prevented behaviour occurs. The removal regex carries the g flag because OUTBOX_TRACK_ONLY_CHOKEPOINT_GUARD marks two blocks, one per repository implementation; an earlier revision removed only the first and so proved half the feature while reporting success. The one guard without a control, BOARD_CAPACITY_TRACK_ONLY_EXCLUSION_GUARD, lives in packages/db and cannot be imported as source by an app test without violating the db-client-boundary check; it is proven by premise assertion plus a positive control instead, which is weaker and labelled as such.
runtime_proof.known_limitations: The DatabaseOutboxRepository chokepoint is measured against a faithful stub Supabase client rather than real Postgres. A dedicated live-DB proof test was written and withdrawn: registering it requires editing docs/05_operations/db-writer-classification.json, which is outside_allowed_paths for lane runtime, and this lane's authorization forbids widening lane authority. Separately, teams and player_team_assignments are empty in production and staging, so the search-backed branch of the coverage guard is not exercised against real rows; the catalog-backed branch is what carries the refusal today.
